key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D plus machine learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar cell stacks and pinpoint high-efficiency, lead-free architectures.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical design rule set for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL choices to accelerate development of scalable, environmentally friendlier perovskite solar cells.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device combinations with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen stacks.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance via Spearman correlation, and the best verified devices reached 28.85% and 28.62% PCE.
watch_item: Model recommendations depend on the representativeness of the training subset, so extrapolation to materials outside the sampled design space should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
